FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R01 Example
Ruby Backend Engineer
r01@example.test

SUMMARY
Product engineer focused on transactional services for small subscription businesses. Comfortable tracing a customer-visible defect through application code and database state before proposing a repair. Prefers small changes with explicit rollback instructions and readable tests. Has worked with product owners, support specialists and designers who do not share the same time zone. Describes operational trade-offs in writing and treats payment correctness as a product requirement rather than an implementation detail.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Ruby, Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL, RSpec, Redis, Sidekiq, Git, Go (coursework only)

EXPERIENCE
Ruby Backend Engineer — Fictional R01 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Built Ruby on Rails billing endpoints with explicit transaction boundaries, idempotency keys and recovery paths for interrupted subscription changes.
- Designed PostgreSQL schemas and reviewed SQL query plans before adding indexes to a slow invoice reconciliation workflow.
- Wrote RSpec request and model tests for failed payments, duplicate submissions and concurrent account updates.
- Diagnosed application performance regressions using request traces and database measurements, then verified fixes against representative production-like data.
- Reviewed pull requests for correctness and maintainability, explaining alternatives to colleagues before accepting changes.
- Coordinated releases through asynchronous design notes and written handovers with colleagues in three time zones.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2017-07 to 2022-12
Maintained order-processing services at Fictional Orchard Systems. Investigated support tickets, reproduced data inconsistencies in a sandbox and added targeted regression tests before changing behavior. Took part in release reviews and helped replace manual database edits with audited administrative workflows. Learned to distinguish a temporary mitigation from a durable repair and documented follow-up work for the next iteration.

PROJECTS
Implemented a personal sandbox for Redis caching and Sidekiq background jobs, including retry behavior and duplicate-message handling. This project uses synthetic subscription records and is not described as professional delivery.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2016. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Go appears only in the skills inventory after an introductory course; no Go project or professional use is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R02 Example
Python API Engineer
r02@example.test

SUMMARY
Backend developer building business APIs for internal operations teams. Works from acceptance criteria and failure examples instead of treating a successful HTTP response as the whole feature. Enjoys making validation rules explicit and helping callers understand rejected requests. Collaborates with interface developers but does not claim professional ownership of browser applications. Uses test fixtures with invented customer records and writes migration notes so another engineer can reproduce a deployment.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, pytest, Docker, OAuth2, Django (self-study)

EXPERIENCE
Python API Engineer — Fictional R02 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Implemented Python FastAPI endpoints for a scheduling service, including request validation, pagination and consistent error responses.
- Created PostgreSQL tables and SQL queries for appointment conflicts, using transactions to prevent duplicate reservations.
- Added pytest integration tests covering invalid requests, database failures and repeated delivery of the same operation.
- Integrated OAuth2 authentication and checked resource ownership before returning account-specific API records.
- Packaged services in Docker and maintained deployment checks that exercised the running health endpoint after release.
- Wrote API documentation and operational handover notes that allowed support engineers to reproduce common failures.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2022-01 to 2022-12
Worked as an associate developer at Fictional Lantern Services. Fixed defects in data validation and built small import scripts under code review. Paired with a database engineer when schema changes affected existing records. Supported weekly releases by preparing reproducible examples, confirming the rollback procedure and keeping issue descriptions current. Used feedback from support staff to improve error messages.

PROJECTS
Built a local service simulator that returns delayed responses and temporary failures. Used it to check retry boundaries in an API client without contacting real external systems. Stored fixture records in an isolated development database.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2021. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Django is self-study only. No Kafka, streaming platform or production event-processing experience is stated.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R03 Example
React Interface Engineer
r03@example.test

SUMMARY
Frontend specialist working on browser-based administrative products. Translates uncertain user requests into small interaction changes that can be evaluated with designers and support staff. Pays attention to keyboard behavior, loading states and recoverable errors as well as the normal journey. Has experience working with API teams through written contracts. Does not present frontend work as ownership of database operations or production backend services.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Jest, Testing Library, Next.js (learning)

EXPERIENCE
React Interface Engineer — Fictional R03 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Built React search and editing screens with predictable component state and explicit handling of delayed API responses.
- Implemented semantic HTML forms and responsive CSS layouts that remained usable on narrow screens and older supported browsers.
- Fixed keyboard focus and screen-reader announcement defects after accessibility reviews, then documented the expected interaction behavior.
- Wrote Jest and Testing Library tests for form validation, failed submissions and restored application state.
- Investigated web performance using browser traces, splitting a costly bundle and checking the impact on loading and interaction.
- Worked with designers and support colleagues to translate user feedback into testable acceptance criteria and iterative interface changes.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2018-06 to 2022-12
Delivered browser interfaces at Fictional Cedar Studio. Maintained shared form patterns and reviewed component changes for unintended effects in other screens. Used version control and peer review for all releases. Prepared clear bug reports with device details and reproduction steps rather than guessing at a browser defect. Helped another developer understand the distinction between visual polish and usable interaction.

PROJECTS
Created a TypeScript component library for a fictional community booking service. Published examples for loading, empty and error states and kept a small visual checklist alongside automated interaction tests. The library has no real users or customer data.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2017. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Next.js server rendering is learning only. No delivered server-side rendering project is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R04 Example
Vue Product Engineer
r04@example.test

SUMMARY
Interface developer focused on maintaining understandable product screens as requirements change. Works well with an established design vocabulary and asks for concrete examples when a feature request is ambiguous. Comfortable reducing a large interface change to a sequence of reviewed improvements. Has owned frontend debugging and component behavior but has not maintained production Rails or Python services. Values written decisions that make later maintenance less dependent on a particular person.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Vue.js, JavaScript, semantic HTML, CSS, Vitest, Git, GraphQL (reading only)

EXPERIENCE
Vue Product Engineer — Fictional R04 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Implemented Vue.js components for inventory browsing, preserving selection and validation state across related screens.
- Built browser interfaces using JavaScript, semantic HTML and CSS with documented behavior for unavailable network responses.
- Wrote automated component tests in Vitest for keyboard actions, validation messages and asynchronous loading transitions.
- Used browser profiling to diagnose performance problems in a large table and verified the revised rendering behavior.
- Managed Git branches and reviewed merge requests so interface releases could be traced to an approved change.
- Recorded technical decisions and progress asynchronously for product and engineering colleagues working different schedules.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2021-09 to 2022-12
Maintained a small customer portal at Fictional Harbor Workshop. Converted design examples into reusable interface components and fixed browser-specific defects under supervision. Collaborated with a backend engineer to agree request shapes and error messages. Built confidence by documenting assumptions, asking for review early and checking related screens before declaring an issue resolved.

PROJECTS
Built a local component catalogue with reusable form, navigation and notification patterns. Documented intended component usage and checked that examples handled long labels and missing values. The catalogue is a personal demonstration rather than a commercial design system.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2020. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
GraphQL is reading only, without an implementation. No professional React experience is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R05 Example
Rails and Vue Fullstack Engineer
r05@example.test

SUMMARY
Generalist product engineer who follows a change from interface behavior through service logic and persistence. Most experience is in small product teams where the same engineer helps clarify requirements, implement a feature and investigate its behavior after release. Uses explicit contracts between screens and APIs. Describes both implementation work and collaboration without assuming every tool in a team repository was part of personal responsibility.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Ruby on Rails, Vue.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, PostgreSQL, RSpec, Cypress, GitLab CI

EXPERIENCE
Rails and Vue Fullstack Engineer — Fictional R05 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Implemented Rails service logic for an equipment reservation product, including safe state transitions and rollback of failed operations.
- Built JavaScript interfaces with semantic HTML and CSS to display availability, conflicts and actionable validation errors.
- Connected browser screens to backend API contracts and coordinated error handling across the interface and service boundary.
- Added RSpec service tests and Cypress browser tests for the same reservation journey, including cancellation and repeated submission.
- Investigated performance across browser requests and database calls, separating slow rendering from repeated server queries.
- Owned a feature from written proposal through implementation, review, release notes and support handover.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2017-02 to 2022-12
Worked on an internal asset register at Fictional Finch Works. Implemented small changes across views and controllers with guidance from a senior maintainer. Added migration notes when data shape changed and reviewed user-facing terminology with operations colleagues. Learned to reproduce a reported issue at the correct layer and to keep proposed fixes small enough for useful review.

PROJECTS
Built Vue.js screens for a fictional lending catalogue, using a Rails API and synthetic records. Set up GitLab CI to run service and browser tests against a disposable database. Documented how to inspect a failed pipeline locally.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2016. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
No Python backend or React delivery is claimed. Work arrangement and availability are not inferred from this technical history.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R06 Example
Python and React Fullstack Developer
r06@example.test

SUMMARY
Product developer comfortable making coordinated changes to a browser interface and a small API. Experience comes from an operations application with a modest, well-defined user group rather than a large public platform. Works with issue descriptions, review feedback and release checklists to make changes reproducible. Will ask for a security review when a feature changes access boundaries. Does not claim expertise in infrastructure ownership simply because the application is containerized.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, pytest, Playwright, OAuth2, Docker, Redis (self-study)

EXPERIENCE
Python and React Fullstack Developer — Fictional R06 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Built Python FastAPI endpoints for case-management workflows with explicit validation and documented failure responses.
- Implemented React forms that preserved user input during failed requests and displayed server-side validation clearly.
- Designed PostgreSQL tables and SQL joins to keep case history consistent during concurrent updates.
- Wrote pytest API tests and Playwright browser tests for the same case creation and amendment workflows.
- Implemented OAuth2 login and resource authorization checks so users could only access assigned case records.
- Built Docker images and maintained deployment smoke checks with documented rollback instructions for application releases.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2021-04 to 2022-12
Supported internal tools at Fictional Willow Operations. Reproduced reported defects using invented records and corrected validation logic under review. Helped maintain a release checklist covering configuration, database changes and user-visible behavior. Joined product discussions to clarify which errors could be retried and which required a user to change their input.

PROJECTS
Developed a personal React and Python planning application with a local database. Kept an API contract document and examples of malformed requests. The demonstration does not implement a distributed cache, high-availability cluster or production traffic handling.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2020. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Redis is self-study only. No direct user research interviews or professional Ruby on Rails work are claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R07 Example
Application Security Engineer
r07@example.test

SUMMARY
Application security practitioner who works with software teams to turn findings into reproducible fixes. Distinguishes an observed vulnerable path from a theoretical risk and explains exploit prerequisites without exposing customer records. Experience includes reviewing authorization boundaries and helping teams evaluate remediation options. Prefers a small regression test and a clear root-cause explanation to a long list of unverified scanner findings. Works only within explicitly authorized assessment scopes.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Secure code review, threat modeling, OWASP, HTTP, Burp Suite, Semgrep, Python, Ruby (reading only)

EXPERIENCE
Application Security Engineer — Fictional R07 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Performed manual security code reviews of account-management services and traced authorization decisions across controller and persistence boundaries.
- Led threat modeling discussions for new integrations, documenting trust boundaries, abuse cases and practical mitigation options.
- Reproduced and triaged vulnerability reports, agreed severity with maintainers and verified remediation before closing the finding.
- Mapped OWASP application weaknesses to concrete fixes and explained why input validation alone did not replace authorization.
- Investigated HTTP request behavior with an intercepting proxy and explained how protocol handling affected an identified vulnerability.
- Worked with developers to create focused security regression tests and wrote remediation notes that a maintainer could apply independently.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2016-08 to 2022-12
Reviewed internal applications at Fictional Juniper Assurance. Prepared assessment scopes and tested only agreed environments. Learned to capture minimal evidence, avoid storing sensitive records and distinguish a product defect from an unsupported deployment assumption. Presented findings to engineers and service owners, including uncertainties and reasonable remediation choices rather than claiming every observation was equally severe.

PROJECTS
Built a Semgrep-based security check for a fictional training application and added CI checks for intentionally vulnerable examples. Maintained false-positive notes and negative fixtures so a clean result was not interpreted as proof of security.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2015. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Ruby is reading only; no professional Ruby development is claimed. No security incident on-call history is supplied.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R08 Example
Security Incident Response Engineer
r08@example.test

SUMMARY
Security operations engineer supporting investigation and recovery during authorized internal incidents. Comfortable organizing uncertain evidence into a timeline and communicating what is established, suspected or still unknown. Works with application and infrastructure owners to choose containment steps that consider service continuity. Experience is primarily operational rather than source-code assessment. Keeps investigation notes concise enough that another responder can resume work without relying on an informal handover.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Incident response, log analysis, AWS, Splunk, runbooks, Linux, Python (coursework)

EXPERIENCE
Security Incident Response Engineer — Fictional R08 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Handled incident response for suspicious account activity, coordinating containment, recovery and follow-up verification with service owners.
- Used Splunk log analysis to correlate authentication events and construct a timestamped investigation timeline.
- Investigated AWS audit records and cloud access configuration to identify the scope of an unauthorized credential use.
- Maintained response runbooks with evidence-preservation steps, escalation contacts and explicit checks before closing an incident.
- Participated in an incident on-call rotation, handing over open investigations and documenting actions taken during each shift.
- Communicated incident status and remaining uncertainty to technical responders and non-technical service stakeholders.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2020-11 to 2022-12
Worked as a monitoring analyst at Fictional Alder Operations. Reviewed alerts against documented investigation steps and escalated cases that required deeper access. Improved notes when an alert did not explain what evidence was missing. Learned to preserve timestamps, distinguish a detection from an incident and avoid taking disruptive containment actions without the correct incident owner.

PROJECTS
Conducted a lab forensic investigation of a deliberately compromised Linux virtual machine, preserving an image and reconstructing process and network activity. This was a training exercise, not a claim of commercial digital-forensics casework.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2019. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Python is coursework only. No manual application code review, Ruby development or threat-model facilitation is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R09 Example
Site Reliability Engineer
r09@example.test

SUMMARY
Reliability engineer supporting services where operational changes need a clear failure and recovery story. Enjoys turning repeated incident work into documented procedures and then into measured automation. Looks for symptoms experienced by users rather than treating every infrastructure metric as an alert. Works with application teams to agree service objectives and safe deployment steps. Separates service reliability experience from feature development or specialist application security review.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Linux, Terraform, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana, Shell, Go (reading only)

EXPERIENCE
Site Reliability Engineer — Fictional R09 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Troubleshot Linux service failures by inspecting processes, resource usage and network behavior before applying a documented mitigation.
- Managed Terraform changes with reviewed plans and isolated state, documenting the recovery path for failed infrastructure updates.
- Operated Kubernetes workloads with readiness probes, resource requests and controlled rollouts for application services.
- Built Prometheus monitoring and Grafana dashboards around user-visible symptoms and service-level objectives.
- Participated in production on-call, coordinated incident mitigation and led follow-up reviews that identified preventable failure modes.
- Maintained operational runbooks and practiced recovery procedures with application owners in scheduled exercises.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2016-03 to 2022-12
Administered internal services at Fictional Birch Hosting. Investigated unreliable deployments and replaced undocumented terminal commands with reviewed configuration changes. Helped application engineers understand resource exhaustion and persistent storage behavior. Learned to preserve enough diagnostic evidence for a later review while prioritizing a safe recovery. Prepared maintenance notices and checked that another operator could follow the same instructions.

PROJECTS
Built Shell automation that provisions a disposable test environment, runs a health probe and tears it down safely. Added a dry-run mode and documented prerequisites so a lab script could not be mistaken for a production deployment tool.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2015. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Go is reading only. No professional Vue, React or Rails feature implementation is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R10 Example
Delivery Automation Engineer
r10@example.test

SUMMARY
Development operations engineer helping product teams release small application changes consistently. Experience is centered on build tooling, test environments and diagnosing pipeline failures rather than ownership of a large production cluster. Documents assumptions about credentials, configuration and artifact versions so failures can be reproduced. Works with developers to reduce manual handoffs without bypassing review. Values a clear release record and a usable rollback path over a pipeline that appears green but never checks the running service.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
GitLab CI/CD, Python, Docker, Linux, secrets management, Terraform (self-study)

EXPERIENCE
Delivery Automation Engineer — Fictional R10 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Built GitLab CI/CD pipelines that tested changes, produced versioned artifacts and deployed the exact reviewed application revision.
- Managed separate development and test environments with documented configuration differences and disposable fixture records.
- Wrote Python automation for environment setup and smoke checks, with actionable exit messages for failed prerequisites.
- Implemented secrets handling through protected environment variables and restricted deployment permissions instead of embedding credentials in scripts.
- Diagnosed delivery failures by separating build errors, missing configuration and unsuccessful runtime health checks.
- Documented release and rollback procedures and walked a second engineer through a recovery using the written instructions.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2022-05 to 2022-12
Supported engineering tooling at Fictional Meadow Products. Maintained small scripts, fixed reproducible environment setup issues and helped colleagues understand failed checks. Used peer review for automation changes and logged assumptions about system permissions. Joined release retrospectives to identify where a manual instruction could become a safe, testable step rather than another undocumented command.

PROJECTS
Packaged a fictional API in Docker and added local smoke checks for its configuration and health endpoint. Kept a clean build context and verified that the container could run as a non-root user. No orchestration cluster was used.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2021. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Terraform is self-study only. No Kubernetes operations or production incident on-call rotation is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R11 Example
Data Pipeline Engineer
r11@example.test

SUMMARY
Data engineer building repeatable flows from operational systems to analytical datasets. Starts with source behavior, record grain and recovery requirements before choosing a transformation. Comfortable investigating late data and explaining why a successful job does not necessarily mean its output is complete. Works with analysts to document definitions and expected use. Does not claim that familiarity with SQL automatically establishes application backend or distributed streaming expertise.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, SQL, ETL, Airflow, data quality, Snowflake (coursework), Git

EXPERIENCE
Data Pipeline Engineer — Fictional R11 Product Team | 2023-01 to 2026-11
- Wrote Python data-processing code for incremental imports with explicit checkpoints and repeatable recovery after a failed extraction.
- Used SQL to reconcile source and target record counts and investigate unexpected duplicate business keys.
- Built ETL pipelines that preserved source identifiers and documented the transformation from operational records to analytical tables.
- Orchestrated dependencies and safe retries in Airflow, including backfill procedures for late-arriving source data.
- Added data quality checks for missing keys, duplicate records and broken joins before publishing tables to analysts.
- Maintained source-to-target documentation and explained dataset grain and known limitations to data consumers.

Earlier engineering role — Fictional Training Organization | 2018-01 to 2022-12
Supported reporting imports at Fictional River Analytics. Replaced manual spreadsheet transfers with reviewed scripts and documented which fields could legitimately be absent. Worked with analysts to reproduce inconsistent totals and discovered cases where a join changed the intended record grain. Learned to separate a source correction from a transformation defect and to preserve an inspectable reconciliation record.

PROJECTS
Built an analytical warehouse demonstration with incremental tables and dimensional data modeling for a fictional library. Included deliberate duplicate and late-event fixtures, documented expected results and checked that rerunning a load did not duplicate records.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2017. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Snowflake is coursework only. No Kafka, streaming platform operation or production web API development is claimed.

FICTIONAL BENCHMARK RECORD — NOT A REAL APPLICANT
R12 Example
Analytics Engineer
r12@example.test

SUMMARY
Early-career analytics engineer turning defined business questions into understandable analytical tables. Works with established conventions and seeks review when a new model changes record grain or access rules. Experience includes maintaining documentation and helping users distinguish a metric definition from a dashboard presentation. Comfortable investigating a failed data check and describing its consequence. Does not claim ownership of distributed ingestion platforms or senior architecture decisions.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
SQL, dimensional modeling, data testing, metadata, dbt, Python (learning)

EXPERIENCE
Analytics Engineer — Fictional R12 Product Team | 2025-01 to 2026-11
- Built SQL transformation models that joined operational records at an explicitly documented business grain.
- Implemented dimensional models with separate fact and dimension tables and described how changing dimensions affected reporting.
- Added data tests for key uniqueness, missing values and relationships, investigating failures before releasing revised models.
- Maintained metadata and column documentation so analysts could identify lineage, definitions and known source limitations.
- Worked with finance and operations stakeholders to clarify a business question and agree which records belonged in its metric.
- Applied secure data-handling rules by restricting sensitive columns and documenting approved analytical uses.

Earlier engineering role / supervised placement — Fictional Training Organization | 2024-06 to 2024-12
Completed an analytics placement at Fictional Acorn Services before moving into the current junior role. Updated documentation under review and reproduced reported discrepancies using anonymized training records. Learned to ask whether two reports used the same population and time period before comparing totals. Supported colleagues by preparing examples that made a definition disagreement concrete.

PROJECTS
Created a dbt demonstration for a fictional bookshop with source declarations, model documentation and relationship tests. Supplied a small invented dataset and expected reconciliation totals. The project runs locally and has not been operated as a production warehouse service.

EDUCATION
Fictional Institute of Applied Computing — computing diploma, 2023. This educational record is invented for testing.

SCOPE NOTES
Python is learning only. No production Airflow orchestration or independently operated ETL platform is claimed.
